paragraphs.dominant_move: optimize signs and name the threats

organization_logic.macro_structure: Summary gives the order of three tools. The body builds a hand graph, rejects pure shortest paths, bounds a cut, guesses hidden exits, then simulates people, then writes the same blocking idea as an ODE. Sensitivity asks what the clock actually depends on. Comparison assigns each model one job. The recommendation is a search the museum should run.
organization_logic.dominant_pattern: Heuristic, then the reason it fails, then a model that can see the failure, then a hedged action.
organization_logic.section_coupling: Section 3.6 lists the gaps section 4 is built to fill. Section 5 says its blocking term is the agent model's refused move. Section 9 does not claim either model found the signs.
organization_logic.argument_quality: Strong on scope and on refusing a naive policy. Weak on calibration: t_0 and c never appear as numbers, and the ODE is confessed as untuned.
human_organization_signals: One would imagine but here we mean
global_organization_chain: nearest exit is only a guess
a thin cut isolates one wing
head count and doors matter, room mix does not
hand the museum a search and a bound

section_progressions.positive_pattern: Known object, crowd, leave and arrive.

analytical job: flood fill, event queue, edge reversal

analytical job: read when congestion peaks and which factor drops out

handoff: the comparison says which model earned which claim

main_argument_chains.claim: Nearest-exit signs are a reasonable first plan and not yet a plan to install.
support_steps: The summary calls the rule a heuristic guess.
Pure shortest paths send responders into the crowd.
The agent model can score other signings.
The recommendation asks for a search rather than reporting one.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The museum should treat nearest-door as the start of a search, not as the posted plan.

main_argument_chains.claim: Clearance time depends on how many people, how many doors, and whether the plan stays connected, not on which rooms start full.
support_steps: Time rises with density and falls as exits are added.
A Mona Lisa reweighting of fifteen rooms does not move the total.
Cut links hurt sharply at high density.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Collect head count, door count and connectivity before spending effort on a room-by-room census.

warnings.warning: mu = t_0 exp(c rho) increases with density. The prose says mean transfer time increases and movement gets harder. The scalar ODE uses exp(-c rho). If mu is the exponential rate, the printed sign speeds people up.

The prose says n(1) = 1, but n_i = (1/t_0) exp(-c rho)(3-2 rho) rho^2 equals 1/t_0 exp(-c) at rho = 1, not 1. The same exponential already multiplies the scalar flow, so a combined step may apply it twice.
The Cheeger interval is also printed as Phi_G = 0.1115026 +/- 0.1056103. That notation reads as a measured center. It is only the midpoint of a bound two orders of magnitude wide.
